# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 28 (Bu-Vb Sk28)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk28
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 28
**Title (English, from literature):** Not receiving with attention on the almsbowl
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-sk28
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pattasaññīpaṭiggahaṇa-sikkhāpada* is the twenty-eighth training rule (*sekhiya*) in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule forms part of the training guidelines governing monastic table manners and deportment during the receipt of almsfood, stipulating that a monastic should receive almsfood with mindfulness and attention fixed upon the almsbowl [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Direct parallels within the Pali canon include the corresponding rule in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*sekhiya* 28), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*sekhiya* 28), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*sekhiya* 28), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra chapters [SuttaCentral]. In cross-tradition Vinaya literature, curated parallels are preserved in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition (*sekhiya* 43 for monks and *sekhiya* 45 for nuns) and the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchā* (*sekhiya* 26), alongside resembling rules documented across the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mahāsaṅghika, and Lokottaravāda traditions [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects dense Pali-internal alignment with neighboring *sekhiya* rules—notably *sekhiya* 32, 31, 4, 30, and 43—accounting for standardized formulaic framing shared across the monastic etiquette sections [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
